slides.heading: What it is
paras: Open-source scanners (a smartphone Orbiter rig, a Raspberry Pi handheld LiDAR, LingBot-Map's video-to-3D) now produce a usable mesh of the thing you need to fit.
slides.alt: DejaViewed carousel, slide 2 of 9. The idea. What it is. Open-source scanners (a smartphone Orbiter rig, a Raspberry Pi handheld LiDAR, LingBot-Map's video-to-3D) now produce a usable mesh of the thing you need to fit. From @itsnicconley · @rawmechatronics · @nateherkai.

slides.alt: DejaViewed carousel, slide 3 of 9. The claim being tested. Output proof: a whole device shipped as code + BOM + printable STL. via @itsnicconley.

slides.heading: What a pro would do that you didn't ask for
paras: A mechanical design engineer would start with an error budget, not a scan: scanner accuracy, mesh-to-primitive fitting error, printer dimensional error, and the clearance they want, each measured.

slides.heading: How you know it worked
items: The physical fit on each real object, judged against a go/no-go criterion written before printing.
Caliper measurements of printed contact features versus CadQuery parameters, within the coupon-derived tolerance.

scale from the ChArUco board or a reference cube in frame.
